evaluation.comparison_note: Identical 149 eligible test observations on held-out battery B0006. The simple linear cycle-trend baseline achieves lower RMSE (7.073 pp) and MAE (6.537 pp) than XGBoost and deep sequence models. Deep sequence models show negative R² due to cross-cell distribution shift.

proxy_notice: Research estimate only. This comparison evaluates dataset-level capacity-retention models from cycle history on NASA PCoE battery cells. It is not personalized to an individual battery or vehicle and is not certified physical SOH.
limitations: The target is each NASA battery's capacity divided by its own first positive measured capacity; it is an operational proxy, not a certified physical SOH reference.
Evaluation uses one unseen test battery (B0006), with 149 scored observations after 19-cycle warmup.
On the same test rows, linear cycle-trend baseline RMSE (7.073 pp) is lower than XGBoost RMSE (8.481 pp), LSTM (10.761 pp), CNN-LSTM (12.127 pp), and GRU (13.906 pp).
Deep sequence models yield negative R² on unseen cell B0006, honestly reflecting cross-cell domain transfer limitations.
NASA README and battery-specific discharge protocol cutoff descriptions differ; the local source did not resolve that discrepancy.
